source.filename: 2018-Modeling of grasping force for a soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness.pdf

actuation: thermal-induced SMA fiber with contraction in length (SMA-1, NiTi alloy, BMF150)
tendon-like pulling wire wrapped around pulleys to generate bending torque
constitutive_assumptions: Planar bending deflection is confined to the XOZ plane because the second moment of area Iy is significantly smaller than Ix (Iy << Ix)
Stretch and compression along the centerline of the soft finger are neglected (linear rate of change vl(s) = [0, 0, 1]^T)
Distributed external moment along the length of the rod is zero (tau = 0)
Distributed external force along the finger is solely due to gravity (f(s) = rho * A * g * eg)
Grasped objects are assumed to be rigid cuboids with vertical planar contact boundaries represented by X = H
Contact mechanics between the fingertip and the grasped object follow an ordinary Coulomb friction model (F_f = mu * F_N)
Linear elastic constitutive moment-curvature relationship for rod bending (m_y(s) = E * Iy * theta'(s))
Equivalent composite bending stiffness formulated as EIy = E3 * I3 + 4 * E2 * I2
Poisson's ratio is assumed to be 0.3, resulting in an effective shear modulus of G = E / 2.6
control_variables: Effective working length of SMA-2 and SMA-3 wires (L2 = L3 = 100 mm)
Diameter of SMA-1 wire (0.15 mm) and nominal length (1200 mm)
Diameter of SMA-3 wire (0.6 mm) and Young's modulus (56 GPa)
Lever arm of the pulling force (d = 8 mm)
Spacing between parallel SMA-2 wires (l_SMA = 4.5 mm)
Number of fingers in the gripper (N = 2)
Baseline Young's modulus of unheated SMA-2 at ambient temperature (E2 = 25 GPa)
Numerical shooting algorithm convergence tolerance (e_H = 0.1 mm), grasping force step size (0.01 N), and torque step size (1 Nmm)
dependent_variables: Normal grasping force (F_N) of the soft finger and gripper
Fingertip position coordinates (Xp, Zp) and vertical offset displacement (Delta Z)
Fingertip position error (ep) between theoretical simulation and experiment
Grasping force error (e_F and e_Fmg) between model prediction and experimental measurement
Maximum sustainable object gravity / payload weight before slip (F_mg = F_f)
No-load initial contact torque and critical detachment bending torque

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Structural decoupling of bending actuation and variable stiffness mechanisms is realized using separate shape memory alloy elements: an electrothermal contracting SMA-1 fiber for bending actuation, thermal-induced SMA-2 wires without length change for variable stiffness, and a superelastic SMA-3 central wire for elastic restoration.

The response characteristics of the soft finger backbone do not comply with constant-curvature models when subjected to combined gravity, grasping contact forces, and driving torques, necessitating a Cosserat rod theory formulation.

Increasing the Young's modulus of the SMA-2 variable stiffness wires from 25 GPa to 48 GPa via electrical heating increases the maximum grasping force of the soft finger by 48.7% experimentally and 42.5% in simulation.
Increasing the object offset distance H from 30 mm to 60 mm increases the required no-load bending torque to reach contact but decreases the attainable maximum grasping force.

Finite element modeling in ABAQUS showed close agreement with the Cosserat rod formulation, exhibiting grasping force differences between 0.005 N and 0.032 N across object offsets from 30 mm to 60 mm at a bending torque of 20 Nmm.

Discrepancies observed between initial multi-finger gripper simulations and experiments were demonstrated not to stem from force closure failure or internal pulley friction, but from surface wear on 3D-printed PLA fingertips that lowered the contact friction coefficient from 0.426 to 0.335.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: experimental hypothesis testing and error analysis

experimental_setup: Two-finger soft robotic gripper mounted on a 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) base bed with PLA finger brackets spaced at 20 mm to prevent wire kinking
SMA-3 superelastic core wire (0.6 mm diameter) providing structural backbone and elastic return
Four SMA-2 wires (0.5 mm diameter) fixed in parallel to SMA-3 without length change, connected to an electrical DC power supply (0 to 1.70 A) for thermal stiffness variation
Single 1200 mm U-shaped SMA-1 wire (0.15 mm diameter, Toki BMF150) routed through fingers and pulleys to provide bilateral bending actuation powered by an independent DC current supply (0 to 0.36 A)
Force sensor to measure tendon pulling force (F_p) and tip contact normal force (F_N)
Graded background scale and graph paper setup for tracking fingertip deflection coordinates (X, Z)
3D-printed hollow PLA test boxes with adjustable internal masses used to determine maximum liftable gravity (F_mg)
Comparative noncompact gripper configuration with four ball-bearing pulleys and adjustable inextensible insulating wire used to isolate internal pulley friction effects
future_work: Optimizing and controlling the soft robotic gripper system to manipulate heavier objects based on the grasping force model
Conducting future experimental investigations on friction coefficients across diverse fingertip contact surfaces and materials
independent_variables: Heating current applied to the SMA-1 actuation wire (0 to 0.36 A), corresponding to driving torque (Td) or pulling force (Fp)
Heating current applied to the SMA-2 variable stiffness wires (0 A, 0.73 A, 1.70 A), setting Young's modulus E2 (25 GPa, 37 GPa, 48 GPa)
Object offset distance H along the X direction (tested at 20 mm, 30 mm, 40 mm, 50 mm, and 60 mm)
Fingertip contact surface condition and friction coefficient mu (fresh PLA at 0.426 vs. rubbed/worn PLA at 0.335)
Mass / gravity of the grasped object (F_mg)
limitations_inferred: The modeling and experimental evaluations are restricted to two-dimensional planar bending in the XOZ plane, leaving 3D out-of-plane torsional or lateral deflections unmodeled
Objects are restricted to rigid flat cuboids; compliance, curvature, and geometric irregularities of grasped objects are not represented in the formulation
Thermal dynamics, heat dissipation rates, cooling transition latencies, and hysteretic behavior during cycling of the SMA wires were not incorporated into the static model
Closed-loop real-time force feedback control was not demonstrated on the physical prototype, relying instead on static position-based (Z offset) estimation and open-loop thermal actuation
limitations_stated_by_authors: The Cosserat-based grasping force formulation is highly nonlinear and lacks an analytical closed-form solution, requiring iterative shooting numerical computations

Model predictive errors increase markedly when bending torque exceeds 40 Nmm or deflection offset Z exceeds 55 mm because large deformations near the critical bending torque cause complex nonlinear responses that cannot be easily modeled
Direct closed-loop feedback control of pulling force using a sensor is difficult because the SMA-1 wire is wrapped tightly around pulleys inside a cavity too small to accommodate a force sensor
Electrothermal contraction of SMA-1 exhibits an inherently nonlinear response that complicates controller design
Friction coefficients at the fingertip degrade over repeated grasping trials due to surface wear on the 3D-printed PLA, leading to modeling mismatches if static friction values are assumed
main_results: A Cosserat theory-based static grasping model was successfully formulated and quantitatively validated for a soft finger and two-finger gripper under complex external loadings including gravity, contact normal force, friction, and actuation torque

Thermal activation of embedded SMA-2 wires increased their Young's modulus from 25 GPa to 48 GPa, yielding a 48.7% increase in measured maximum grasping force (42.5% in simulation) at an object offset of 50 mm

Increasing object offset H resulted in higher required no-load initiation torques (from 4 Nmm at H = 30 mm to 9 Nmm at H = 60 mm) and reduced maximum grasping forces (from 0.676 N at H = 30 mm to 0.265 N at H = 60 mm)
ABAQUS FEM static analysis confirmed the validity of the Cosserat model with discrepancies limited to 0.005 N - 0.032 N across offsets from 30 mm to 60 mm under 20 Nmm torque

Experimental testing with a low-friction ball-bearing noncompact gripper disproved internal pulley friction/force closure failure as the origin of gripper model discrepancy; updating the friction coefficient to account for PLA surface wear (mu = 0.335) reduced prediction errors below 0.04 N
modeling_methods: Cosserat rod theory (formulating planar equilibrium of a 1D rod under tip point forces, bending moments, and distributed gravity)
Classical Coulomb friction law for fingertip-object contact mechanics
Numerical shooting method / iterative step-adjustment algorithm using step sizes Delta F_N = 0.01 N and Delta T_d = 1 Nmm with an error tolerance e_H = 0.1 mm
Finite element method (FEM) static simulation in ABAQUS for validation
performance_metrics: Normal grasping force (F_N, measured in N)
Percentage increase in maximum grasping force due to variable stiffness activation (48.7% measured, 42.5% simulated)
Maximum payload gravity sustained before slippage (F_mg, measured in N)
Fingertip position error (ep in mm) and grasping force error (e_F and e_Fmg in N)
No-load initiation torque and critical detachment torque (in Nmm)
possible_gap_implications: The absence of active thermal-electric dynamic modeling and integrated force sensing suggests that future research could focus on embedded micro-sensing and active cooling schemes to enable closed-loop force control and faster cycling times

The reliance on planar Coulomb contact mechanics against rigid flat surfaces indicates a need to investigate spatial 3D Cosserat contact mechanics for conformable grasping of soft, delicate, or irregular geometries
paper.research_objective: To develop, model, and experimentally validate a grasping force model based on Cosserat rod theory for a soft robotic gripper featuring structurally decoupled SMA actuation and variable stiffness mechanisms, enabling quantitative prediction and tuning of grasping forces under varying stiffness, object offsets, and surface friction.
paper.research_problem: Conventional constant-curvature models cannot accurately predict the grasping force and deflection of soft robotic fingers subjected to complex loads such as gravity, driving torques, and contact forces; moreover, compact variable stiffness soft grippers typically suffer from coupling between actuation and stiffness-tuning mechanisms, or lack adequate load capacity.
stiffness_mechanism: thermal-induced SMA wire without change in length (four SMA-2 NiTi wires whose Young's modulus transitions from 25 GPa to 48 GPa via phase transformation upon Joule heating)
stress-induced SMA fiber with super elasticity (SMA-3 NiTi core wire providing base elasticity and elastic restoration)
structural decoupling of variable stiffness mechanism from actuation mechanism
paper.title: Modeling of grasping force for a soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
